## Milestone 1 - Task 3.2: HTTP Executor

Consumes the API Request Contract produced by 02-api-request-builder (docs/contracts/api-request-contract.md), executes it with n8n's native HTTP Request node, and returns the standard HTTP Response Contract (docs/contracts/http-response-contract.md).

This workflow only *executes and captures* the response - it never compares against `expected`, never decides PASS/FAIL, and never calls an AI model. That is the Decision Agent's job (docs/architecture/milestone-1.md section 5), out of scope here.

Invalid input, an unreachable target, or a timeout all produce the shared ERROR payload (docs/contracts/error-payload.md) instead - never silently dropped, never thrown in a way that kills the rest of the batch.

## Task 3.2 design notes

- `Apply Authentication` is the only node that reads a real credential (from this workflow's own environment variables, e.g. API_AUTH_BEARER_TOKEN) - the API Request Contract's `authentication` field only ever carries a strategy marker, per ADR 002 and docs/contracts/api-request-contract.md.
- The HTTP Request node is configured with `neverError` so 4xx/5xx responses are captured as normal data (`status_code` on the response contract), not thrown as node errors. Genuine execution failures (DNS, connection refused, timeout, malformed URL) route through the node's error output into `Build Network Error Payload` instead.
- `Route Validation Errors` skips the HTTP Request node entirely for items that already failed validation, so this workflow never attempts to send a request built from an invalid contract.

nodes.name: Response Normalizer
nodes.notes: Hand-off boundary to the Response Normalizer workflow (Task 3.3, not yet built). Receives either an HTTP Response Contract (docs/contracts/http-response-contract.md) or an ERROR payload (docs/contracts/error-payload.md). No response normalization or pass/fail comparison happens in this workflow.
